title: Coexistence of long- and quasi-long range spatial order in 1D quantum quasicrystals
authors: A. Mendoza-Coto, M. Grossklags, J. Stefaniak, T. Donner, F. Piazza
abstract: Quasicrystals exhibit long-range positional order without periodicity, arising from multiple incommensurate wave vectors. In self-assembled quasicrystals, the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance gives rise to two Goldstone modes-phonons and phasons-associated with two competing wave vectors. Here, we demonstrate a unique scenario exclusive to quasicrystals: a mechanism that gaps out only one Goldstone mode (associated with one wave vector), while the other remains gapless. In one dimension, this leads to the coexistence of long-range order at the gapped wave vector and quasi-long-range order at the gapless one, due to sustained fluctuations. We show that this phenomenon can be realized using ultracold bosonic atoms in optical cavities.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates 1D quantum quasicrystals realized using ultracold bosonic atoms in optical cavities. By analyzing the low-energy excitations, the authors demonstrate a unique mechanism where selective gapping of Goldstone modes allows for the coexistence of true long-range order and quasi-long-range order simultaneously. This provides a novel platform to study complex ordering phenomena beyond standard periodic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the unique physical scenario in one-dimensional quantum quasicrystals where Goldstone modes can selectively gap, leading to a coexistence of true long-range order and quasi-long-range order.
main_result: The system exhibits distinct ordering regimes: true long-range order is found at the gapped wave vector component, while quasi-long-range order persists at the remaining gapless component due to sustained fluctuations.
method: The analysis employs a combination of spectral variational methods and the coherent-state path-integral formalism to derive an effective hydrodynamic action for low-energy excitations.
model_or_system: The model is a quasi-one-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) trapped in an optical cavity, whose interactions are engineered via laser-painted potentials to mimic quasicrystalline coupling.
key_observables: Gap structure of Goldstone modes (gapped vs. gapless), phase correlation functions ($\langle\hat{\delta}_1\hat{\delta}_1angle$, $\langle\hat{\delta}_2\hat{\delta}_2angle$), and the excitation velocities ($c_\pm$).
important_parameters: The coupling parameters ($\kappa_2$) controlling mode hybridization, system size ($L$), and the ratio of incommensurate wave vectors ($\Gamma = k_2/k_1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a 1D reduction from transverse dimensions and relies on approximations within the hydrodynamic regime for low-energy excitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup using cavity QED, ground-state phase diagrams showing transitions between phases (H and QC), and space-time local density behavior under propagating long-wavelength excitations.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the effective quadratic action for fluctuations ($\delta S$) in the hydrodynamic limit. It then analyzes the resulting dispersion relations, identifying three modes: one gapped mode ($\omega_1 \propto q^2$) and two gapless modes ($\omega_\pm \propto q$). Finally, it calculates correlation functions to confirm the distinct ordering regimes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges concepts from quantum optics (cavity QED implementation) with advanced condensed matter physics (quasicrystals), providing a concrete platform for studying exotic many-body order parameters in ultracold atom systems.
